# Game model (Locksmith-like box-into-lock puzzle)

## Board
- 512x512 image, 16x16 grid of 32px cells. col = x/32, row = y/32.
- Background light gray #CCCCCC with 8px grid lines.
- Bottom pink strip = move/time budget bar (64 cells of 8px); ~1 dark cell per 3 actions
  (i.e. ~192 actions). Fills dark from the RIGHT.

## Entities
- PLAYER: 1 cell, green #4FCC30 with an 8px WHITE strip on one side = FACING direction.
- BOX: 1 cell, blue center in a frame. Frame #333333 = idle, #666666 = attachable now
  (i.e. player is adjacent on the box side and FACING it).
- HELD BOX: renders white with blue center; sits in the cell the player faces; moves
  rigidly with the player (relative offset fixed while held).
- LOCK: blue rectangle (w x h cells) with hollow gray #999999 interior. Player and held
  boxes pass through freely.
- ORANGE solid cell (#FF851B): appeared in level 2; role not yet known.

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move up/down/left/right one cell.
  - If the target cell is free: player moves AND turns to face that direction (turning
    only happens when NOT holding a box).
  - If the target cell is blocked: player does NOT move but DOES turn to face that
    direction (free rotation trick).
  - While HOLDING a box, moving does NOT change facing; the pair translates rigidly.
- ACTION5 = pick up the box in the faced cell (if frame is gray) / drop the held box
  into the faced cell (if empty).
- No RESET/undo offered mid-level.

## Goal (confirmed level 1)
- Fill EVERY interior cell of the lock with a box. Level completes the instant the last
  cell is filled (progress +1, next level loads).

## Efficient technique
- Carry the box on the side facing the travel direction is NOT required; the box keeps a
  fixed offset. To deposit a box at cell T while travelling left, pick it up facing LEFT
  (stand at box_col+1) and stop at T_col+1, then ACTION5.
- Fill order matters: the player must stand in the cell adjacent to the target on the
  side opposite the facing; so fill the far cells first (e.g. fill (3,r) before (4,r)
  when depositing leftwards).

# Game model (Locksmith-like: carry boxes into the lock)

## Board
- 512x512 image, 16x16 grid of 32px cells. col = x/32, row = y/32.
- Background light gray #CCCCCC with grid lines.
- Bottom pink strip = per-level action budget (64 cells of 8px, drains from the RIGHT).
  Drain rate VARIES per level (L1 ~1 cell/3 actions => ~190 actions; L2 ~0.91 cell/action
  => ~70 actions). CHECK THE BAR EARLY and plan a short route.

## Entities
- PLAYER: 1 cell, green #4FCC30 with an 8px WHITE strip on one side = FACING direction.
- BOX: 1 cell, blue center with frame. #333333 idle, #666666 = attachable right now
  (player adjacent and facing it), #000000 = claimed by the orange bot.
- HELD BOX: white with blue center; keeps a FIXED offset from the player (the cell the
  player faced when picking up) and translates rigidly with the player.
- LOCK: blue rectangle with hollow gray #999999 interior; both player and boxes pass
  through freely. Cells = outer size in 32px cells.
- ORANGE BOT (#FF851B): 1 cell, moves 1 cell per player action. It seeks boxes, carries
  them to the lock and deposits them (helps you). It CANNOT be picked up. You CAN steal
  a box it is carrying (grab it when the box lands in the cell you face).

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = up/down/left/right one cell.
  - Free target: player moves and (only when NOT holding a box) turns to face that way.
  - Blocked target: player does not move but STILL TURNS. (cheap 1-action rotation)
  - Holding a box: facing never changes; blocked moves do nothing.
- ACTION5 = pick up box in the faced cell (needs #666666 highlight) / drop held box there.
- Resolution order: the player's action resolves FIRST, then the orange bot moves.

## Goal (confirmed L1 & L2)
- WIN = every blue box has been deposited inside the lock. Lock cells may remain empty
  (L2 finished with 5 boxes in a 6-cell lock). Level ends the instant the last box drops.

## Planning rules
- To deposit a box at cell T, the player must stand at T minus the hold offset, so choose
  the pick-up facing to match the approach direction.
- A held box blocks on obstacles too; plan the box's lane as well as the player's.
- Fill cells so that already-placed boxes never block the lane of later ones
  (e.g. travelling leftwards along a row, fill the leftmost cell first).

# Level 4 (attempt 1 notes - likely timing out)
Map: chamber wall (hatched) ring: rows 5 & 11 cols 5-10, cols 5 & 10 rows 5-11.
Interior cols 6-9, rows 6-10. Player starts (7,8).
Inside boxes: (6,6),(8,6),(9,6),(8,9),(6,10),(9,10). Outside box (6,1).
Bots start: (14,1), (2,3), (6,14).
Lock cells (7): (1,6),(1,7) | (2,9) | (14,5) | (13,7) | (9,14),(10,14).
Black solid walls: col 7 rows 0-4; diagonals (4,12),(3,13),(2,14),(1,15) and
(11,12),(12,13),(13,14),(14,15).
Budget this level ~ 0.63 bar-cells per action => ~100 actions total.

KEY FACTS LEARNED
- A held box can be pushed into ANY hatched wall cell and dropped there ("slot");
  bots on the other side then fetch it. Player cannot enter wall cells.
- Bots FAILED to collect boxes from TOP wall slots (6,5) and (8,5) (they parked
  above them and froze). Slots on the LEFT wall (5,10), RIGHT wall (10,10) and
  BOTTOM wall (8,11) were collected fine.
- A bot will not pick a box while the player stands adjacent to it AND faces it.

BETTER PLAN FOR NEXT ATTEMPT (do NOT use top wall slots):
 - (8,9) -> bottom slot (8,11): from (7,8) R to (8,8), ACTION2(rotate), pick, D,D, drop  [6]
 - (9,10)-> right slot (10,10): ACTION4 rotate(blocked), pick, R, drop                  [4]
 - (6,10)-> left slot (5,10): L,L to (7,10), pick, L, drop                               [5]
 - (6,6) -> left slot (5,6): go (7,6) facing left is impossible directly; instead
   from (6,10) go up to (6,7), pick facing up, ... better: stand (7,6) facing left,
   pick (6,6), move L -> box into (5,6), drop.
 - (8,6) -> right slot (10,6): stand (7,6) facing right, pick (8,6)... box would hit
   (9,6). Do (9,6) first: stand (8,6)?? occupied. Simplest: (9,6)-> right slot (10,6)
   via stand (8,6)... occupied by box.
   Order: first (9,6): stand (8,7), rotate up? no - use (9,7) facing up? that gives
   hold-up (top slot - BAD). Instead: pick (9,6) from (8,6)? occupied.
   => Move (8,6) box down into interior first, then handle both from the side.

# Level 4 - map + retry plan (attempt 1 ran out of budget)

MAP (32px cells): chamber wall (hatched) ring rows 5 & 11 cols 5-10, cols 5 & 10 rows 5-11.
Interior cols 6-9 rows 6-10. Player starts (7,8) facing up.
Inside boxes: (6,6),(8,6),(9,6),(8,9),(6,10),(9,10).  Outside box: (6,1).
Bots start (14,1),(2,3),(6,14).
Lock cells (7): LEFT (1,6),(1,7),(2,9) | RIGHT (14,5),(13,7) | BOTTOM (9,14),(10,14).
Black solid: col 7 rows 0-4; (4,12),(3,13),(2,14),(1,15); (11,12),(12,13),(13,14),(14,15).
Budget ~0.63 bar-cells/action => ~100 player actions.

RULES CONFIRMED
* Player may push a HELD box into any hatched wall cell and drop it (a "slot").
  Bots on the outside then fetch it. Player can never enter wall cells.
* Bots do NOT collect from TOP wall slots (they park above and freeze). Left/right/
  bottom slots work (bot may take 3-6 turns to start).
* A bot won't take a box while the player is adjacent to it AND facing it.
* The bot ferry is the bottleneck: put each box in the wall slot NEAREST its lock.

TARGET DISTRIBUTION (7 boxes / 7 lock cells)
  outside box (6,1) -> a LEFT lock (bot does it automatically)
  2 boxes -> LEFT wall slots (5,r)   -> locks (1,6)/(1,7)/(2,9)
  2 boxes -> RIGHT wall slots (10,r) -> locks (14,5),(13,7)
  2 boxes -> BOTTOM wall slots (c,11)-> locks (9,14),(10,14)
DO IT EARLY so bots have time.

SEQUENCE (player from (7,8)):
 1. (8,9)->bottom (8,11): A4 (to 8,8); A2 rotate; A5 pick; A2,A2; A5 drop        [6]
 2. (9,10)->right (10,10): A4 rotate; A5; A4; A5                                  [4]
 3. (6,10)->left (5,10): A3,A3 (to 7,10); A5; A3; A5                              [5]
 4. (6,6)->left (5,6): A1x3 (to 6,7); A4 (7,7); A1 (7,6); A3 rotate; A5; A3; A5   [9]
 5. (8,6)-> move into interior (8,7): to (8,7) via (7,6)->(7,7)->(8,7);
    A1 rotate; A5; A2; A5 drop                                                    [7]
 6. (9,6)->right (10,6): go to (8,6) via (7,6); A5 pick(facing right); A4; A5     [7]
 7. box (8,7)-> bottom: from (9,6) A3 to (8,6); A2 rotate; A5; A2 x4; A5          [8]
 Total ~46 actions, then park at (7,8)/(8,8) oscillating (never adjacent+facing a slot).

# LEVEL 4 (attempt 2+) — KEY INSIGHT & EXACT PLAN

## Map (cells, col,row)
Chamber ring (hatch = blocks PLAYER and BOTS, but a HELD box may sit/pass over it):
outer cols5-10, rows5-11. Interior = cols6-9, rows6-10. Player start (7,8) facing UP.
Boxes: A(6,6) B(8,6) C(9,6) D(8,9) E(6,10) F(9,10); outside box (6,1).
Bots: (2,3) LEFT, (14,1) RIGHT, (6,14) BOTTOM. Bot speed = 1 cell per player action.
Locks: LEFT (1,6),(1,7),(2,9) | RIGHT (14,5),(13,7) | BOTTOM (9,14),(10,14).

## CRITICAL: map is split into 3 sealed regions
Black bar col7 rows0-4 + chamber + diagonal black staircases seal LEFT, RIGHT and
BOTTOM pockets from each other. A bot can only deliver to locks in ITS region.
=> Must place exactly: 2 boxes in LEFT wall slots (col5), 2 in RIGHT wall slots (col10),
2 in BOTTOM wall slots (row11, cols6-9). Outside box (6,1) is the 3rd LEFT box.
Attempt 1 failed only because 3 boxes went right / 1 bottom -> last box unusable.
AVOID TOP slots (row5): bot dithered ~27 turns before collecting one.

## Carry rule
Hold offset = facing at pickup. Offset right -> can only drop in col10 slots;
offset left -> col5; offset down -> row11; offset up -> row5.
Blocked move (no box held) = free rotation.

## EXACT SEQUENCE (36 actions) from fresh start
A: A1, A1, A3(rot), A5, A3, A5            -> box (5,6); P(6,6) faceL     [6]
B: A4, A5, A2, A4, A4, A5                 -> box (10,7); P(9,7) faceR    [12]
C: A3, A1, A4(rot), A5, A4, A5            -> box (10,6); P(9,6) faceR    [18]
F: A2, A2, A2, A5, A2, A5                 -> box (9,11); P(9,10) faceD   [24]
D: A1, A1, A3, A2(rot), A5, A2, A2, A5    -> box (8,11); P(8,10) faceD   [32]
E: A3, A5, A3, A5                         -> box (5,10); P(6,10) faceL   [36]
Then A4 (leave (5,10) slot un-faced) and idle by oscillating around (7,9)/(7,8)
(never stand adjacent+facing a filled wall slot: bots may refuse to pick).
Budget ~100 actions total; expect all 7 deliveries by ~action 50-60.

[After action · write GUIDE.md]
# Game model — "Locksmith": deliver every box into blue locks

## Board
- 512x512, 16x16 grid of 32px cells: col = x/32, row = y/32.
- WIN = every box is inside blue-bordered lock cells (lock cells may remain empty;
  boxes outnumber-or-equal check is on boxes, not cells).
- Bottom pink bar = action budget (64 cells). Drain rate varies per level
  (0.3–1.0 cells/action → 64–210 actions). MEASURE IT in the first 2–4 actions:
  sample y=504..511 with 64 columns at level start and after N actions.

## Entities
- PLAYER: green, 8px white strip on the facing side.
- BOX: blue center; dark frame idle, lighter frame = attachable (adjacent + faced),
  black frame = claimed by a bot, white body = currently held.
- LOCK: blue rectangle; its cells are walkable and sample as #727272.
- ORANGE BOT: helper. Moves 1 cell per player action, hauls any box outside a lock
  into the lock. Efficient pathing; parks when it has no target.
- PURPLE THIEF: adversary. Same movement; hauls boxes OUT of locks into its own gray
  zone (gray = #727272 block without blue border).
  *** KEY: face it and press ACTION5 → the thief is CAPTURED/removed permanently. ***
  It highlights YELLOW when it is grabbable.
- HATCHED (striped) cells: walls for player and bots, but a HELD box may be moved over
  them and dropped there; a bot on the far side can then pick it up. Use hatch cells as
  pass-throughs between sealed regions.

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = up/down/left/right. Free target: move (and turn, when not holding).
  Blocked target: no move but STILL TURNS = free rotation (only when not holding).
- ACTION5 = pick up / drop the box in the faced cell; also captures a purple thief;
  it is a harmless no-op when the faced cell is empty (useful "wait" action).
- Resolution order each turn: player acts first, then all bots move.

## Carrying
- Hold offset = the facing direction at pickup and NEVER changes while held.
  offset left/right → box travels in your row; up/down → box travels in your column.
- To drop a box into target cell T you must stand at T minus offset, so pick with the
  offset that matches your intended approach; plan the BOX's lane as well as your own.
- Fill far lock cells first so placed boxes don't block later lanes.

## Tactics that won levels
1. Capture every purple thief early — otherwise deliveries are undone forever.
   Ambush recipes (player acts first, so a thief standing in the cell you face is caught):
   - Stand adjacent to the cell it must enter, already facing that cell, and wait (ACTION5).
   - Block a 1-wide corridor / maze exit so it cannot advance, then ACTION5.
   - Thieves also pause a turn when picking up or dropping — being adjacent then is enough.
2. Sealed regions: map walls first. A region's boxes can only be served by agents inside it,
   or via hatch drop-offs. Distribute boxes so each region gets exactly as many boxes as it
   has lock cells (level 4 was lost by sending 3 boxes to a 2-cell region).
3. Bots do the long hauling for free (they move only when you act), so never idle if you can
   haul; idle only with in-place no-ops (blocked move or ACTION5) when waiting for a delivery.
4. Stage/handoff points: put boxes 1 cell from a bot's route to shorten its round trip;
   the makespan is max(player work, bot work), so balance them.

[After action · message]
**Game complete: 9/9 levels, terminal state WIN.**

Final level summary (level 9, ~62 of ~64 budget actions):
- Mapped the board, found the col‑9 wall, the hatched band sealing the upper‑right pocket, and the bottom maze.
- Delivered the two right‑side boxes myself, then dropped a third **into the hatched wall** so the sealed‑in bot could collect it.
- Raced west and **trapped the purple thief in the maze exit corridor (3,9)/(3,10)** and captured it before it could steal anything.
- Hauled the far box from (1,8) into the 3×3 lock, then idled in place (blocked‑move no‑ops) while the helper bot deposited the final box.

Key insights discovered during the run and now stored in `GUIDE.md`:
- Purple thieves can be **grabbed with ACTION5** (they highlight yellow) — this permanently removes them and was the crux of levels 6–9.
- Held boxes can be pushed **into hatched wall cells** to pass boxes between sealed regions.
- Blocked moves are free rotations; ACTION5 on an empty cell is a free "wait", which is essential for ambush timing since the player always resolves before the bots.
